review_notes: I read the whole file. It has about 76 near-identical membership lemmas about `.fv`. Each one is proved by hand-sequenced `rw [fv_…]`, `with_reducible rw [Finset.mem_union]` and `Finset.mem_erase` steps. I then checked where the `fv_*` lemmas are declared. CompactSyntaxFV.lean marks `fv_syn_wa`, `fv_syn_wex`, `fv_syn_wrex`, `fv_syn_cnin`, `fv_syn_ccompl`, `fv_syn_cphi` and `fv_syn_wbr` as `@[simp]`. CoreFVSimp.lean marks `fv_class_cv`, `fv_class_cab` and `fv_wff_classMem` as `@[simp]`. CompactSyntaxFVExplicit.lean has no simp attributes at all (my count was 0). This file opens CompactSyntaxFVExplicit and CoreFVSimp, not CompactSyntaxFV, so the unannotated Explicit versions are the ones in scope. I did not run Lean, so I can't say whether `simp` would close each goal. In particular I haven't checked how the `mem_lt_freshVar` side goals behave. The finding is limited to the simp-interface gap. Lemmas of the form `x ∈ A ∪ A` (for example 0156, 0160 and 0196) could also be handled by `Finset.union_self`. I did not report that separately.

findings.problem: The `fv_*` computation lemmas that this file uses are the unannotated copies in `CompactSyntaxFVExplicit` (`fv_syn_wa`, `fv_syn_wex`, `fv_syn_wrex`, `fv_syn_cnin`, `fv_syn_ccompl`, `fv_syn_cphi`, `fv_syn_wbr`). None of them is `@[simp]`, and the file does not open `CompactSyntaxFV`, which has the identical statements marked `@[simp]`. So the simp set is split. `CoreFVSimp` and `CompactSyntaxFV` mark these `.fv` equations simp, while the Explicit namespace, which this file and other proofs use, withholds the attribute. Because of this, about 76 lemmas in the file are proved by hand-ordered `rw`/`left`/`right` chains. `with_reducible rw [Finset.mem_union]` and `Finset.mem_erase` are applied step by step, with the `left`/`right` choices encoding the exact syntactic shape of the term. Any change to the generated syntax (for example the order of union arguments in `fv_syn_wbr`) breaks these proofs. The goals are all of the form `x ∈ (term).fv`, which is what a simp normal form is for.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the `fv_*` equations in `CompactSyntaxFVExplicit.lean` with `@[simp]`, matching `CompactSyntaxFV.lean`. Alternatively, open the simp-tagged `CompactSyntaxFV` versions here, or add `attribute [local simp]` for them in this file. Keep only one of the two copies of each lemma in the scope that proofs open. Then state the membership lemmas through `simp`, and keep a manual `mem_lt_freshVar` step only where `simp` leaves a side goal. For example `nb055_support_mem_0140` and `0141` become `by simp`. The `Finset.mem_union` rewrites in `0142`–`0161` can also be left to `simp`, with `Finset.mem_union`, `Finset.mem_erase` and `Finset.mem_singleton` as its normal form.
findings.benefit: The same normal form (`Finset.mem_union`, `Finset.mem_erase`, singleton membership) becomes available everywhere the Explicit lemmas are imported, and callers no longer have to know about the duplicate copies. The membership lemmas stop depending on a fixed left/right branch order, so they survive changes to the syntax encodings. Each lemma shrinks from 10–30 lines of `rw` plumbing to a `simp` call plus any freshness side goal.
